items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S2015

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the "New York
immigrant family unity pilot program"; and providing for the repeal of
such provisions upon expiration thereof

PURPOSE:

This bill defines and provides a right to state-appointed counsel in
immigration removal proceedings for indigent detained New Yorkers
being held for deportation proceedings.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 is the title.

Section 2 adds a new section 94-c to the executive law to create a
pilot program to provide counsel to indigent individuals facing
deportation.

Section 3 is the effective date

JUSTIFICATION:

In New York the impact of deportation on families is of particular
significance since over twenty percent of New York State residents are
foreign-born. Deportations can have devastating effects on families
and tear the fabric of communities across the state. Without counsel
it is virtually impossible for detained individuals to avoid
deportation, regardless of whether the individual has a strong claim
for relief or a viable defense. Recently, New York City has started a
pilot program which has shown early successes. This bill is aimed at
providing representation for more New Yorkers and evaluating the
viability of a state-wide program.

This pilot program addresses the compelling need to protect New
Yorkers and New York families against the injustices inherent in the
current deportation system. It is a system where New Yorkers are
locked up and forced to litigate against trained government attorneys
without access to counsel, leading to wrongful deportations and
unnecessarily broken New York families.

Deportations take an economic as well as a human toll on the State of
New York. When New Yorkers are wrongfully deported, families become
dependent on various state services, tax revenue is lost and employers
incur significant disruptions. It makes economic sense to provide
representation to eligible New Yorkers because doing so reduces the
costs that burden New York employers, the state government, immigrant
families", and New Yorkers as a whole.

New York State respects the exclusive province of the federal
government to regulate immigration and the flow of immigrants into and
out of our country. New York State, however, maintains the authority
to provide for the health, safety and welfare of its residents and its


right to protect its residents, communities, and employers. There is
nothing in this act that should be read to conflict with federal law.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014: S7052/A9192 - Finance Committee/Ways & Means Committee

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect April 1, 2016 and shall expire two years
after such effective date.

summary: Creates the New York immigrant family unity pilot program.
